chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from 'Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) issued a ruling regarding a female slave who was a Christian, then she embraced Islam and bore a child for her master. Then her master died and bequeathed her freedom as a concubine during the time of 'Umar. She married a Christian named Dayrani and reverted to Christianity, then she bore two children and became pregnant with a third.

He said: So he ruled that Islam should be presented to her. It was presented to her, but she refused. He said: Whatever child she bore while Christian, they are slaves to the brother whom she bore to her first master.
And I will detain her until she gives birth to the child in her womb. When she gives birth, I will kill her.

This does not contradict the earlier reports, because in this report, her execution was mandated because she apostatized from Islam and married a disbeliever. For this reason, the execution became obligatory upon her.
And if she had not married, her ruling would be to be detained indefinitely, according to what the earlier reports contained.

key_terms.دَيْرَانِي: A specific Christian name or tribe

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a freed female slave who apostatizes and marries a non-Muslim?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ali (AS) in *Al- Istibsar* clarifies the specific legal status of a *Umm al-Walad* (mother of a child) who apostatizes, distinguishing between the penalty of execution for marrying a disbeliever and indefinite detention for mere apostasy. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential nuance that her Christian offspring remain enslaved to her Muslim son, preserving the master's lineage rights, while her detention continues until the birth of her third child to finalize the legal proceedings.
